name: Spaghetti Squash Boats with Chicken

ingredients.buy: 7 medium spaghetti squash, about 2 lb each, halved lengthwise and seeded
1 3/4 tsp kosher salt; scant 1 tsp kosher salt
14 strips thick-sliced center-cut bacon, roughly chopped
3 1/2 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized pieces
7 cups baby spinach, torn into pieces
3 1/2 cups shredded part-skim mozzarella cheese, divided
7 tbsp chopped fresh basil, plus more for serving

writer_notes: 7 spaghetti squash halved = 14 boats = 14 servings, one boat per container. Portioning is one-to-one, no pot-weighing needed beyond evening out the filling.
Source (wellplated) is a 2-squash recipe scaled 3.5x. All conversions in the locked view are internally consistent with a clean 3.5x multiply.
Band check: cal 475 (450-700), carbs 36 (<=40), protein 40.5 (>=40) all pass. Carbs at 36 sit close to the 40 ceiling; in-band but worth an auditor glance.

Source step 1 offloads squash roasting to a linked 'Roasted Spaghetti Squash' recipe. I wrote an explicit roast step that uses the olive oil, salt, and pepper so those bought ingredients are tied to a step (spec-guards hard-fails on orphans). All 11 locked ingredients are used; no step uses anything not bought.

DATA SMELL for repair pass: source lists black pepper TWICE (1/4 tsp for squash + 1/4 tsp for chicken = 1/2 tsp source total). Salt captured both amounts ('1 3/4 tsp; scant 1 tsp'), but locked Black Pepper shows only 'scant 1 tsp' — a single 3.5x amount, suggesting the second pepper application was dropped in the merge. Expected ~1 3/4 tsp total to mirror salt. Prose cites no pepper quantity, so no card fix needed.
Source step 7 has a typo ('until the cheesy is bubbly'); corrected to 'cheese' in the schema steps and prose.
No cost_lines were provided in this dispatch, so shop_smart makes zero per-package cost claims; only {{cost_ps}} in the closing carries a dollar figure.

prose.intro_html:
Here is a plant that spent its whole life pretending to be pasta, and for once we are going to let it win. Roast a spaghetti squash, drag a fork through it, and the inside falls apart into strands that look like noodles and cost like a vegetable. Then we hollow the halves into boats and load them with bacon, chicken, and melted mozzarella. That is the whole trick.

What you get is a plate that eats like comfort food and reads like a spreadsheet win: {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, under 40 grams of carbs, and not a noodle in sight. The squash shell is the plate, the container, and half the meal all at once, which is the kind of efficiency I can get behind.
prose.shop_smart:
The squash is the whole show, so buy well. You want 7 medium spaghetti squash around 2 pounds each. Pick them up before you buy them: a good one feels heavy for its size and has a hard, unbroken skin with no soft spots or mushy stem ends. Pale yellow is fine, deep yellow is fine, just avoid green tinges, which means it was picked early.

Chicken breast is the protein, and 3 1/2 pounds is family-pack territory, so buy the big tray instead of the tidy little one and cut it into bite-sized pieces yourself. For the bacon, get thick-sliced center-cut and do not toss the rendered fat afterward. We keep one tablespoon of it to cook the chicken, so it is doing double duty as your cooking oil.

On the dairy, grab a block of part-skim mozzarella and shred it yourself rather than paying for the pre-shredded bag, and buy plain nonfat Greek yogurt in a tub rather than the little single cups. Baby spinach comes in a bag or clamshell, and a small bundle of fresh basil finishes it. Everything here is a normal grocery run, no specialty aisle required.
prose.make_it:
Start with the squash, because it takes the longest and it is happy to wait on you. Heat the oven to 400 degrees. Halve all 7 squash lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush the cut faces with the olive oil, season with the kosher salt and black pepper, and set them cut-side down on sheet pans. Roast until a fork slides into the flesh easily, then pull them out to cool and drop the oven to 350 degrees.

While that happens, cook the bacon. Heat a large saucepan over medium, add the chopped bacon, and let it crisp and render for about 8 minutes. Lift the bacon out with a slotted spoon onto a paper-towel-lined plate and pat it dry. Pour off the fat but keep one tablespoon in the pan.

Turn the heat up to medium-high. Add the chicken pieces, season with the garlic powder plus salt and pepper, and saute until cooked through, about 5 minutes. Pull the pan off the heat and stir in the spinach until it wilts down, then fold in the Greek yogurt, half of the mozzarella, and the chopped basil. That is your filling.

Now the squash. Once it is cool enough to handle, run a fork through the inside to shred and fluff the strands so they loosen from the walls and make a little nest inside each shell. Divide the chicken filling evenly among all 14 boats, using the fork to lightly mix it into the squash. Arrange the stuffed boats on baking sheets, scatter the reserved bacon and the remaining mozzarella over the top, and bake at 350 until the cheese is bubbly, about 10 minutes. Let them rest a few minutes, then finish with a little more fresh basil.
prose.portion_html:
This one portions itself, which I love. Seven squash halved gives you 14 boats, and 14 boats is exactly 14 servings, so one boat is one container. No weighing, no dividing a pot, no arguing over who got the bigger scoop.

The only place to be careful is spreading the filling. When you divide the chicken mixture among the boats, eyeball them side by side and even it out so no shell gets shorted, or set a boat on a kitchen scale and aim for the same weight of filling in each one. Cool them fully before you lid the containers so they hold up in the fridge, and they reheat straight in the shell.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is the part that matters. All that bacon and cheese and chicken, and it still comes out to {{cost_ps}} per serving. You are buying a vegetable to be the base of the meal instead of a boxed carb, and the squash quietly does the heavy lifting that pasta or rice usually charges you for.

Fourteen dinners cooked at once, each one hitting its protein number, each one under budget. That is the whole point of cooking in a batch: you pay once, in one afternoon, and you eat all week without thinking about it again.
prose.upsell_html: If a per-serving cost like this is the kind of math you want on every dinner, that is exactly what we do here every single week. Membership runs a dollar a month, and it pays for every recipe, every price-checked shopping list, and every batch plan we put out. Cook one batch like this and it has already paid for itself several times over.

head.description: Spaghetti squash boats stuffed with chicken, bacon, spinach, and melted mozzarella. A budget high-protein meal prep dinner that scales to 14 servings with no pasta.
head.keywords: spaghetti squash boats, chicken spaghetti squash, high protein meal prep, budget meal prep dinner, stuffed spaghetti squash, low carb chicken dinner, bacon chicken squash, meal prep chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F. Halve 7 spaghetti squash lengthwise and scoop out the seeds. Brush the cut faces with olive oil, season with kosher salt and black pepper, and roast cut-side down until fork-tender. Set aside to cool and reduce the oven to 350 degrees F.

Heat a large saucepan over medium and add the chopped bacon. Cook until crisp and the fat has rendered, about 8 minutes. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon to a paper-towel-lined plate and pat dry.
Discard all but 1 tablespoon of the bacon fat and raise the heat to medium-high. Add the chicken pieces and season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Saute until cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Remove the pan from the heat and add the spinach, stirring until it wilts. Stir in the Greek yogurt, half of the mozzarella, and the chopped basil.
Once the squash is cool enough to handle, use a fork to shred and fluff the inside flesh so it loosens from the walls and forms a nest.
Divide the chicken filling evenly among the 14 boats, lightly mixing it into the squash with a fork. Arrange on baking sheets and top with the reserved bacon and remaining mozzarella.
Bake at 350 degrees F until the cheese is bubbly, about 10 minutes. Let cool a few minutes, then serve topped with additional fresh basil.
